narrative.overview:
A student's paper planner: quiet ink on cool paper, where the only loud thing on the page is the highlighter stroke across what is due today. The board stays neutral so the owner's own words carry the screen; color appears only where it changes what to do next.

Density is moderate. Four equal columns hold cards with one or two lines of text and a single line of quiet metadata. The interface uses the Windows system face and follows the Windows light or dark setting, so it reads as a native tool, not a website. Motion exists once: a card that reaches Done gets a short highlighter swipe, so finishing something registers.
keyCharacteristics: Restrained palette: cool neutrals, one ink-blue accent for actions and focus, one highlighter yellow for "today".
Tonal layering instead of borders: background, then column panel, then white card.
One type family at four sizes; weight, not size, carries emphasis.
Every state has a visible form: hover lift, focus ring, drag marker, empty-state hint.

rules.name: The One Highlighter Rule
rules.body: Highlighter yellow marks two things only: what is due today, and, for 700ms, a card that has just reached Done. A third use dilutes the signal the owner scans for.

rules.name: The Measured Contrast Rule
rules.body: Every text and fill pair meets WCAG AA (4.5:1) in both themes, and input borders meet 3:1. The lowest text pair is the overdue chip in dark mode (4.63:1).

rules.name: The Lift Means Movable Rule
rules.body: Only things you can drag or that float above the board get the raised shadow.

dos: Do keep highlighter yellow for "due today" and the Done swipe only.
Do use `ink-2` for secondary text instead of lowering opacity.
Do give every new interactive element a hover state, the ink-blue focus ring, and a keyboard path.
Do write empty states that say what to do ("Drag here what you'll do today.").
donts: Don't add a second accent color or color-code sources; source icons stay in faded ink.
Don't put borders around cards; the tonal step and the Card shadow separate them.
Don't add motion other than the Done swipe and short state transitions.
Don't insert outside text (emails, messages, events) with `innerHTML`.
